domains.title: Ontology Schema Design and Workflow Assembly

objectives.title: Model object types, properties, interfaces, shared properties and value types
Choose stable identity, cardinality and meaningful link types
Assemble operational workflows across Ontology, Workshop, Functions, Actions and Automate
Understand impact and evolve the schema without breaking consumers
Choose declarative edit rules or a function-backed Action
Configure parameters, validation, submission criteria and forms
Configure side effects, notifications and webhooks
Reason about Action security layers and troubleshoot rejected Actions
Choose between TypeScript, Python and AIP Logic
Query, aggregate, traverse links and edit objects safely
Version, publish and consume Functions
Test Functions and diagnose common failures
Design pages, sections, layouts, widgets and conditional visibility
Design variable, filter and event flows
Connect Workshop to Ontology data, Actions, Functions and AIP
Diagnose stale or slow modules, publish safely and preserve module interfaces
Register applications, configure OAuth, scope resources and generate the OSDK
Choose user-based or service-based authentication without exposing secrets
Fetch, paginate, aggregate, invoke Actions and use REST APIs
Diagnose scopes, authentication failures, stale SDKs, rate limits and deployment issues
Select triggers, conditions and evaluation modes
Configure effects, execution modes, ownership and scope
Design for retries, repeated events, duplicate effects and race conditions
Test automations safely and diagnose failures
Configure prompts, typed inputs and outputs, tools, blocks, agents and AI-backed Actions
Give AI the minimum data and capabilities, and decide when AI adds value
Use evaluations, traces and execution history, and review AI-generated code
Apply roles, organizations, markings, restricted views and branch protection
Separate application and resource access from data access
Understand user-scoped and project-scoped execution and service identities
Monitor application, Ontology, pipeline and automation health
